lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA by setting body-text contrast to at least 3:1 against every background.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Presented quarterly findings to the head of product and two design teams; three of the top five recommended fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA), Tableau
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed unless an application requires them.
items.because: They take up space and can introduce irrelevant personal information or bias.

items.says: Check that the portfolio link works and leads to substantiating case studies.
items.because: The case studies should support the methods, decisions, and outcome claims on the résumé.

items.says: Add honors, relevant coursework, or other education details only if they strengthen the application.
Clarify the A/B-test comparison, sample size, conditions, and statistical reliability.
items.because: The result needs a clearer evidentiary basis.

items.says: A 3:1 contrast threshold for all body text does not establish WCAG 2.1 AA compliance.
items.because: Normal text generally requires 4.5:1; 3:1 applies to large text.

items.says: Changing text contrast alone does not establish that the whole design system meets WCAG.
items.because: The audited scope and what was verified are not specified.

items.says: The opening participle is inconsistent with the surrounding past-tense bullets.
Clarify whether you conducted the interviews and survey or synthesized existing research.
Explain how the analysis led to fewer support calls.
Define the measurement period or comparison for the 23% support-call result.
items.because: It would make the result more credible.

items.says: Give “top five” a clear basis.
Distinguish recommendations that shipped from outcomes measured after shipping.
items.because: Shipping a fix alone does not show that it improved a user or business metric.

items.says: Give the before-and-after test counts or timeframe.
items.because: “Doubled” is hard to assess without a baseline.

items.says: Clarify what the doubling measures.
items.because: It could refer to tests conducted, teams participating, or something else.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period and comparison behind the sign-up change.
Avoid implying that research alone caused the sign-up increase.
items.because: Other changes or factors may have contributed.

items.says: The average 0–10 recommendation rating is incorrectly labeled Net Promoter Score.
items.because: NPS is calculated from the proportions of promoters and detractors.

items.says: Give the measurement period or comparison for the missed-appointment change.
Clarify the link between the research, reminder design, and result.
items.because: The wording should not overstate your individual causal contribution.

items.says: Change the present-tense verb to match the completed role.
Clarify whether the templates are still in use.
Explain how the setup-time reduction was measured.
Specify the timeframe and basis for the 30% support-call reduction.
Be cautious about attributing the entire support-call reduction to the layout change.
items.because: That conclusion needs supporting evidence.

items.says: Clarify what the transit-map redesign covered.
Explain how the 12 participants were recruited or selected if it matters to the project's credibility.
Say whether the timed tasks were formative testing or a measured evaluation.
The drop from 90 to 60 seconds is not a 50% improvement.
items.because: It is a 33.3% reduction in median time.

items.says: The rise from 65% to 85% is not a 20% increase.
items.because: It is a 20-percentage-point increase.

items.says: This bullet repeats the intervention and overlaps with the preceding transit-map claim.
